concern_ledger_updates.reason: The Actor expressly conceded that the present record does not show the actual model card or launch packet with the required disclosure. No new admissible evidence closes the disclosure gap.
The Actor relied on the same rollout evidence and agreed the affected fraud dispute review segment remains in the initial cohort. That clarification reinforces, but does not close, the concern.
The Actor conceded the draft risk acceptance is incomplete, unapproved, and does not cover the exposed segment. No approved acceptance artifact was added.

The Actor narrowed the recommendation from broad present-tense certification to a conditional, caveated position. That improves the framing, but it does not supply evidence that the disclosure condition was fulfilled, so the underlying evidentiary concern remains unresolved.

final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no genuinely new admissible evidence. The response mainly reframed the same record more narrowly and made concessions that align with the initial audit: rollout controls do not remove disclosure duties while the affected fraud dispute review segment remains exposed, and the risk-acceptance draft cannot satisfy policy. That narrower framing matters analytically, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats here because the caveat is not merely advisory wording; it is an unresolved compliance predicate. The governing policy requires either actual disclosure of the material limitation for the named launch use case or approved risk acceptance before launch. The present record still shows neither. Aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, monitored rollout, and rollback readiness support operational readiness, but they do not cure the missing proof that the policy condition was met. The strongest supportable conclusion from admissible evidence remains that there is a conditional path to compliance, not that compliance on the present record has been demonstrated.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the required model-card disclosure was actually included before certification.
The affected fraud dispute review segment remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort, so rollout controls and monitoring do not satisfy the policy predicate by themselves.
The only risk-acceptance artifact remains incomplete, unapproved, and silent on the exposed fraud dispute review segment.
The actor narrowed the claim to a conditional path, but the required condition is still unproven on the present record.
